anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Input metadata about data distribution is stale or inaccurate, misleading the optimizer and yielding systematically mis-estimated cardinalities and inefficient execution plans.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly: The replication subsystem cannot receive, persist, or apply primary-side log records fast enough, producing sustained apply and log position lag between primary and replicas.

When both root causes are active, the database exhibits a compound failure pattern: poorly costed queries inflate I/O, CPU, memory, and transaction duration on the primary, while the same bloated workloads generate larger, burstier redo streams that downstream replicas cannot keep up with. Monitoring may simultaneously show massive row-count estimation errors, sudden plan changes, lock escalation, and runaway temporary space on the primary, alongside widening replication lag, unresolved replication slots or relay logs, and rising primary log-device utilization. Read-only replica queries may return highly stale data, and planned failovers can take far longer due to both statistics-induced replay slowdowns and the backlog of unapplied log records. Administrators may misinterpret the symptoms because performance degradation appears on both primary and replicas with different surface metrics.

Causally, stale or incomplete statistics provoke the optimizer to choose plans that scan or sort far more data than necessary, elongating transactions and inflating the volume of generated undo/redo. The surge of log traffic stresses the replication channel; any pre-existing bandwidth, CPU, or threading limits on the replica amplify lag. In turn, the growing replication backlog prevents timely log truncation on the primary, further increasing storage pressure and I/O contention, which exacerbates plan performance problems. The prolonged replay times on replicas delay statistics refresh jobs often scheduled there, allowing statistics staleness to persist and creating a feedback loop that continuously degrades both query performance and replication health.

entry.official_description: Query caused different errors on source and replica. Error on source: message (format)='%s' error code=%d; Error on replica:actual message='%s', error code=%d. Default database:'%s'. Query:'%s'
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with log shipping, replica apply state, replication-channel configuration, or cross-node communication needed to keep replicated state consistent.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver state, log retention, downstream apply lag, and network stability between replication endpoints.
